paragraphs: Friend, here's what I hear in all this: God tells His people exactly how to come near Him. He doesn't leave it to guesses. The burnt offering, the grain offering and the peace offering each have their own steps, and the LORD speaks them from the Tent of Meeting (Leviticus 1:1). A God who gives directions like that wants to be approached, and He wants it done His way.

Now look at what keeps showing up. When a man brings a burnt offering from the herd, he lays his hand on its head so it can be accepted "on his behalf to make atonement for him" (Leviticus 1:4), and the animals from the herd or flock have to be "unblemished" or "without blemish" (Leviticus 1:3, 10; 3:1, 6). Even the grain offering has to be made of "fine flour" (Leviticus 2:1), and the burnt offering is called "a pleasing aroma to the LORD" (Leviticus 1:9). I think the lesson is that coming to God costs something, and He is worth it.

So what do you do with that, baker? You bring Him your best, and you bring it the way He asked, not the way you feel like doing it. Even the salt had its place, because the LORD said to leave out nothing of "the salt of the covenant of your God" (Leviticus 2:13). Hold on, because the LORD isn't finished teaching about offerings yet, so keep those ovens ready.
